entries.title: Docs · Engine bridges
entries.summary: One Forge API contract, three real editor integrations: a Unity UPM package, a Godot addon, and an Unreal plugin, each generating a mesh from a prompt and importing it with the engine's own native glTF pipeline.

entries.title: Docs · Engine QA
entries.summary: A free real-time-engine fitness grade for any 3D model: draw calls, material count, texel density, a per-level LOD triangle budget, and whether the mesh is cheap and closed enough to use as its own physics collider.

entries.title: <agent-3d> gets model-viewer's AR contract: ar-modes, variants, hotspots, and /ar drops the third-party CDN
entries.summary: <agent-3d> now matches the AR/viewer contract the market expects from model-viewer (Apache-2.0): ar-modes picks which launch paths to try (WebXR, Scene Viewer, Quick Look), ar-placement anchors floor or wall, ios-src supplies a pre-baked USDZ or the element generates a best-effort one on device, variant-name switches a GLB's real KHR_materials_variants materials live, and any element with slot="hotspot" tracks a 3D position and flies the camera to a saved orbit on click. /avatars/:id/ar and /agents/:id/ar (pages/ar.html) now run entirely on <agent-3d ar>; the page no longer loads a third-party viewer from a CDN.

entries.title: Animation Studio: trim, loop-blend, and save any generated clip to your library
entries.summary: The Animation Studio's prompt-to-clip flow (type a prompt, generate motion on the self-hosted GPU worker, preview it retargeted onto the loaded avatar) now has an editing and persistence half. The transport grows trim start/end inputs, a loop-blend duration field, and a loop toggle, all recomputed through a non-destructive edit path so the live preview, the GLB export, and the saved clip always agree on the current edit. A Save to library button collects a name and visibility and posts the canonical, pre-retarget clip to the shared clip library, so it plays back correctly on any future rig, not just the avatar it was previewed on. A separate bug that crashed every generated clip's playback the moment it reached the browser (AnimationClip.parse() expected userData as a JSON string, the server was sending an object) is also fixed.

entries.title: Engine QA: a free real-time-engine fitness grade, plus real LOD chains
entries.summary: A new free grade answers the question a game engine's import step asks that neither glTF validation nor simulation readiness does: draw calls, material count, texel density against the mesh's real-world size, a per-level triangle budget for a LOD chain, and whether the mesh is cheap and closed enough to use as its own physics collider. GET/POST /api/3d/engine-qa grades any public GLB (format=stl exports a watertight mesh for printing); the same browser-only checks run with zero network cost in Rig Doctor, and the full grade with a one-click upgrade in the GLB viewer, through a shared <engine-qa> panel component. The underlying LOD builder (packages/glb-tools's buildLodChain, real meshoptimizer decimation tagged with MSFT_lod) is now also available on generation: send { "lods": true } to POST /api/forge and the finished creation gets a combined LOD-chain variant alongside its delivered mesh, the same opt-in, fire-and-forget pattern as the existing web-delivery variant.

entries.title: Every generated and purchased model now ships with a signed provenance credential, free, by default
entries.summary: Content credentials (specs/PROVENANCE_3D.md) used to be an on-demand, Claude-track action: you had to call anchor_provenance to get one. Now every GLB the Forge produces, across every generation lane (free NIM, Forge Pro, rigged avatars, self-host TRELLIS/Hunyuan, async GCP workers), gets an ed25519-signed content credential the moment it's materialized, and every first download of a paid asset from the x402 asset bazaar gets one too, with the hash and a verify link returned right in the download response. Signing and storage are free and local, no Solana write and no spend, so there's nothing to gate; the separate paid anchor_provenance upgrade, which additionally commits the hash on-chain, is untouched and still available. A credential is keyed by content hash, so it's issued exactly once per file no matter how many times a lane or endpoint touches it. Model pages now show the same verified / tampered / unverified badge the 3D viewer already had, and a third party can check any model for free with GET /api/provenance. The owner can turn automatic issuance off platform-wide with PROVENANCE_AUTO_DISABLE=true; nothing else about verification changes if they do.

entries.title: Real VRM avatars: spring bones, expressions, and .vrma clips via @pixiv/three-vrm
entries.summary: The hand-rolled VRM loader is gone. vrm-boot.js now registers the real VRMLoaderPlugin (@pixiv/three-vrm) on the three.ws GLTFLoader, so VRM 0.x and 1.0 avatars get genuine MToon materials, spring-bone physics, node constraints, look-at, and all 18 expression presets, driven live by vrm.update(delta) in AnimationManager and mapped onto the ARKit-52 face-capture driver. VRMAnimationLoaderPlugin loads .vrma clips into the same retargeting pipeline that drives non-VRM humanoids, so a single clip plays on either. The Ready Player Me import page (/import-rpm) now accepts .vrm files alongside .glb, and a long-standing bug that 400'd every import at the final save step (it sent an invalid source value) is fixed. docs/avatar-engines.md upgrades three-vrm from interop to live.

entries.title: Restyle and part edits now prove they kept the rig, not just claim it
entries.summary: Material Studio's AI restyle and seeded colorway variants, plus Restyle Studio's HoloPart "Regenerate part" tool, are now checked against their own source bytes with @three-ws/glb-diff before anything is persisted: a restyle declares it keeps topology, UVs, skeleton, skin, and clips, a part regenerate declares the narrower skeleton-and-clips promise since the part's own shape is meant to change, and the operation throws instead of returning a URL if the real diff shows otherwise. A successful restyle response now carries preserve: { kinds, verified: true } as evidence. Model Diff's underlying engine (packages/glb-diff) grew three independent mesh sub-hashes, topology, uv, and skinWeights, so a caller can tell which kind of change happened instead of one opaque geometry hash, and every lineage step in Restyle Studio that has a parent now shows a "Diff" link that opens Model Diff pre-loaded with that exact before/after pair. Regenerating a part also now mints its own durable lineage version automatically, closing a gap where part edits were not recorded.

entries.title: Text-to-motion gets a second GPU backend: MoMask, selectable per request
entries.summary: The self-hosted text-to-motion worker behind the Animation Studio and POST /api/forge-motion now runs two independent generation backends on the same GPU lane: MDM (Motion Diffusion Model, MIT), the existing default, and MoMask (EricGuo5513/momask-codes, MIT), a residual-VQ tokenizer plus masked and residual transformer that publishes a lower HumanML3D FID (0.045 vs. T2M-GPT's 0.141). Pass model: "momask" to /infer or /api/forge-motion to route a prompt through it instead; omit it and MDM keeps answering as before. Both backends converge on the same (T,22,3) HumanML3D position format and the same shared decode math, so a MoMask clip previews, retargets, and exports exactly like an MDM one. The two projects ship conflicting top-level `utils` packages; the worker resolves that at load time so either backend can be warmed in the same container without the other's modules leaking in. MoMask's checkpoints are staged to production storage and the worker is wired to load them; the first on-GPU deploy and a real in-house benchmark against MDM are tracked as the next step.

entries.title: Three new engine bridges: Unity, Godot, and Unreal, one prompt to a mesh in your editor
entries.summary: A shared contract (specs/ENGINE_BRIDGE.md) and three real, independent implementations: a Unity UPM package that imports with glTFast, a Godot addon that imports with Godot's own native GLTFDocument, and an Unreal plugin that imports through Unreal's Interchange glTF pipeline. Each one calls only the public Forge API (POST /api/forge to submit, GET /api/forge?job=<id> to poll, a plain HTTPS GET to download), the same free-first routing and anonymous x-forge-client auth every other Forge caller gets, with the same four import settings (generate_colliders, import_materials, scale, destination) mapped onto each engine's own equivalent. A dropdown and a Generate button in each editor: type a prompt, get a mesh dropped into your scene.

entries.title: 3D viewers no longer flood the browser console, and /trenches stops hammering an offline feed
entries.summary: Every page with a 3D model viewer moved to model-viewer 4.4.0, the first release that both decodes our compressed avatars and drops the debug lines 4.3 printed for every model on the page. The trenches dashboard now checks the feed once and backs off while it is offline instead of sending five requests every 15 seconds, and desktop app windows no longer trigger a fullscreen-attribute warning.

entries.title: A page for every three.ws app: Android, Solana Seeker, iPhone, desktop and the web desktop
entries.summary: The new Apps hub lists every way to run three.ws, each with its own page: the web desktop, the Android app (APK download), Solana Seeker (live on the dApp Store, Seed Vault sign-in and Genesis Token verification), iPhone and iPad (what runs today and what the native build adds once Apple enrollment clears), and the Windows and Linux desktop app, whose download button reads the live release feed and picks the right file for your system.

entries.title: A registry of every place three.ws is listed
entries.summary: The listings registry tracks 121 surfaces across MCP directories, x402 directories, aggregators, cloud marketplaces, awesome-list pull requests and press, with a command that re-fetches every live entry so a dropped listing shows up.

entries.title: A stuck background job now fails fast instead of hanging for 15 minutes
entries.summary: Every scheduled background job (cron) on the platform now answers cleanly and quickly if something inside it gets stuck, instead of silently hanging until the server's own 15-minute connection limit cuts it off with no explanation. Each job now gets a real time budget matching what it already declared, the status board records the failed run immediately, and an alert fires with the job's name attached so it can be diagnosed in seconds instead of traced by hand from a blank timeout. Image rendering for 3D creations got the same treatment: a stuck browser launch, page load, or screenshot now times out on its own instead of tying up the render queue.

entries.title: An agent set to Grok now answers as Grok everywhere, with a badge when it can't
entries.summary: Profile chat, the agent editor's copilot, scheduled strategy runs, and the gateway all now read an agent's chosen brain through the same resolver, so picking Grok for an agent actually means Grok on every surface, not just the one where it was set. A Grok pick first tries the agent owner's own saved xAI key, then the platform's, before falling back to the free default chain. When Grok genuinely can't answer (no key reachable anywhere), profile chat now shows a small badge naming which model answered instead, so it's never a silent swap.

entries.title: API keys can no longer arm spenders or move payout addresses without the wallet scope
entries.summary: Sixteen routes that accept an API key could arm something that spends or redirect where money lands, for any key at all. They now require the wallet:write scope: the treasury autopilot, the auto-launcher, the market maker, live Oracle watches, the pump buyback and distribute policy, signal subscriptions, recurring agent charges, team tasks that hire paid agents, agent orders and spending mandates, an agent's wallet address, a skill listing's proceeds split, animation payout addresses, a Launchpad page's payout wallet or pricing, and opening or re-terming a vault. Pausing, cancelling and closing stay open to any key, and editing an agent no longer lets a narrow key raise its spend limits or change its payment fallbacks.

entries.title: Auto-rigging now covers non-humanoid meshes, not just Mixamo-shaped ones
entries.summary: The auto-rigging worker behind the Forge's "Animate it" step used to assume a roughly humanoid mesh (a head, a torso, two arms, two legs); anything else, a creature, a prop, a vehicle, came back unrigged. A new fallback worker built on UniRig and SkinTokens (both MIT) now catches those cases: a lightweight shape heuristic in the rigging worker decides whether a mesh is humanoid-shaped, and anything that isn't routes to the new worker for a skeleton and skin weights built for its actual topology instead of forcing a Mixamo bone set onto it.

entries.title: Avatar builds that hit a full library now say so, and the news knowledge base stops losing stories
entries.summary: If your avatar library filled up while a photo or prompt avatar was still generating, the finished job used to sit unresolved and retry in the background without telling you why nothing appeared. It now closes with a clear message: delete an avatar or upgrade, then build it again. News stories whose text contained a half-cut emoji or a stray null character were silently dropped from the knowledge base the 3D agents ground their answers on, about 120 a day; they are now cleaned and saved. Static files such as images and environment maps stop answering a server error when the CDN revalidates them, GPU workers fetch reference photos from hosts that refuse anonymous clients, and a stalled upstream can no longer hold an image or webhook request open until the platform timeout.

entries.title: Browse every feature by goal
entries.summary: A new /everything page groups all 340 product pages under twelve goals (make, animate, build an agent, embed, earn, launch, trade, on-chain, worlds, discover, developer tools, account) with search, pins, recents and a new-this-month feed. The nav leads with it, the command palette labels every result with its goal, and tool pages like Forge, Create and Widgets now end with a what-next strip.

entries.title: Choose which @-mentions your agent answers, right from its editor
entries.summary: An agent's Social tab now has an "Answer mentions" section: turn it on, keep it in dry run while you watch what it would say, cap it at a daily reply count, and pick exactly which kinds of mentions it may act on. A new decisions list on the same page shows the agent's own recent calls, what it decided and why, so the owner never has to ask an admin to check a console on their behalf.

entries.title: Every 3D generation now writes a signed run receipt
entries.summary: Each Studio run (avatars, rigged avatars, meshes, rigs, refinements) records stage by stage what was expected, what was observed, and a verdict: met, recovered by a named fallback, missed with its cause, or skipped. The rig is verified by reading the delivered file back, not by trusting the rigger. Receipts are ed25519-signed, linked from every result, browsable at /runs with stage-by-stage rates, and verifiable offline with one command.

entries.title: Forge adds a lane that hands back an already-rigged model
entries.summary: A new Forge engine, "Rig on generate", predicts a model's mesh, joint skeleton and skin weights together in one pass instead of handing back a bare mesh that still needs a separate rigging step. Built on VAST-AI-Research's AniGen (MIT), running on our own self-hosted worker. Pick it from the engine grid, give it a single reference image, and the finished creation arrives already animatable, with the poll response marking it rigged and reporting its joint count so the UI never offers a redundant rerig call. It is opt-in: generating without picking it behaves exactly as before.

entries.title: Forge gets a fidelity lane: match your photo instead of guessing it
entries.summary: A new Forge engine, "Match my photo", fuses 1 to 4 photos of the same object into one pixel-aligned 3D model instead of generating a plausible guess from a single view. Drop photos into the existing view slots and label each one Front, Back, Left or Right; the model is pixel-aligned to every photo you give it, and more photos narrow the result further. Only one photo on hand? Toggle "fill in the other sides" and the worker synthesizes the missing angles before reconstructing. Built on TencentARC's Pixal3D (MIT) running on Microsoft TRELLIS.2's backbone, with MV-Adapter (Apache-2.0) for the view synthesis step. Every input photo is recorded against the finished model, and single-photo requests on every other engine are unaffected.

entries.title: Live widgets and an assistant on the desktop, and the desktop is back at /
entries.summary: The homepage is the web desktop again, and the Field moves to /?view=field. The desktop gains eleven live widgets: the $THREE price with a 24 hour chart, weather where you are, clock, calendar, the newest agents, Pulse wallet moves, coins launched through three.ws, platform stats, headlines from the news desk, your device's battery, network and storage, and sticky notes. Pin them to the desktop in small, medium or large, drag them on a snap grid, or keep them on the widgets board beside a news column. The new assistant pane answers questions about three.ws, opens the right app from its reply, and lets you switch to any public agent and talk to it instead. Nothing is sample data: a source that is down says so and offers a retry.

entries.title: Menu bar panel for the desktop app
entries.summary: Click the three.ws icon in your menu bar or tray and a small panel shows your agent alive in 3D, its Solana wallet balance, a start and stop button, anything waiting on your approval, unread alerts and a box to ask the agent something. Approvals still open the native confirmation window, so what you approve is exactly what you were shown.

entries.title: Real agents live on the campus: a greeter meets you at the gate and every agent you walk up to talks back
entries.summary: The campus is now populated by the ten most talked-to public agents on three.ws, each wearing its own avatar from its public record (five on a phone). The most popular one stands beside the gate path, turns to you as you walk in, waves and says hello through its own brain. Every agent idles, wanders a step, faces you when you come near and carries a name tag; walk up (or tap the tag) and press E to open a conversation that streams the agent's real reply, shows it as a speech bubble and can read it aloud. The panel opens the agent's profile as a window and hands you the one-tag embed that puts that exact agent, body and brain, on any web page. GET /api/agents/public now returns avatar_model_url for public and unlisted avatars.

entries.title: Restyle Studio can now edit a single part of a model, not just the whole thing
entries.summary: Models with named part nodes, whether from the new "Editable parts" Forge engine (PartCrafter, MIT) or from the existing part-segment tool, now show a Parts panel in Restyle Studio. Select a part and every material tool, presets, AI restyle, manual sliders, scopes to that part alone instead of the whole model. Swap a part in from a local file, or hit Regenerate to send it through the new HoloPart worker (MIT), which completes whatever geometry was hidden or cut off at the segmentation seam, then reassembles the result back into the same model under the same part name. Part node names never change across either path, so a model edited this way stays compatible with every other part-aware tool on the platform.

entries.title: Rig Doctor now diagnoses non-humanoid rigs too, not just naming mismatches
entries.summary: Rig Doctor's canonical-joint coverage score has nothing to say about a creature, prop, or vehicle rig: it has no Mixamo-shaped skeleton to map and always reads as "will not animate" by design. A new Skin weights stat answers the question that actually applies to a rig like that: how many joints influence the single heaviest-weighted vertex, and how many of the mesh's vertices came back with no joint influence at all. Zero unweighted vertices means the skin is sound even though the clip library will never retarget onto it; a nonzero count means part of the mesh will not move under any skeleton.

entries.title: Sentiment Scout's X reads gained a second, independent path through xAI
entries.summary: The Sentiment Scout reads X for posts quoting a coin's exact contract address, as evidence a holder can open and check. When our own X search credentials are unavailable or rate limited, it now fails over to xAI's x_search tool, a second route to the same posts, metered by its own daily cap so an outage on one path never silently costs more than planned on the other. No change for anyone reading the Scout: the evidence looks the same either way.

entries.title: Share a finished Forge creation on X and it plays inline
entries.summary: A link to a finished Forge creation now carries an X player card instead of a flat image: the post expands into the real 3D model, posed with its own poster frame and ready to orbit, through the same safe embed runtime the agent-profile embeds use (no audio or video element, HTTPS assets only). A creation that is still generating keeps the plain image card until it finishes, so a link never promises a model that isn't ready yet.

entries.title: The @-mention reply bot now reports its own status, and /grok shows it live
entries.summary: A new public endpoint, /api/x/mention-bot/status, answers whether the @-mention reply bot is live, in dry run, or paused, how many handles it has replied on, how many replies it sent in the last 24 hours, and its median reply time. No mention text or author identity is included. The /grok page now shows this as a live section, and /api/healthz carries the same signal as a platform subsystem, so an operator sees a wedged reply queue or a rising error rate within the hour it starts, instead of the bot quietly going silent with no signature anywhere.

entries.title: The campus is now a real place: daylight, walk-in buildings, photographic surfaces and real props
entries.summary: The 3D campus in front of the desktop is rebuilt to feel like walking through a real place rather than a dark game level. A physical sky and sun with soft shadows that follow you, hills on the horizon, a walled gate with lamps and a welcome sign, a lawn, concrete paths and a paved plaza. Every building is a room you walk into through its door: the brick office with a gabled roof, windows and a furnished desk; the marble-columned exchange with a ticker outside and over the dais inside; the forge with a glowing furnace; the gallery under a skylight, hanging the real avatars of the agents on the campus; a hillside mine with a timbered portal, rails and a cart; the launchpad with its rocket, gantry and crew cabin; a pergola plaza with a fountain; and a timber market hall with striped stalls. Walls, floors and roofs use CC0 photographic materials from Poly Haven, and trees, hedges, lamps, benches, bins, crates and barrels are real glTF models streamed from the three.ws object library, nearest first. Walls and furniture are solid for you and the agents, the camera never cuts through a wall, teleporting puts you at a building's door facing in, and quality adapts to the device (a software renderer always gets the lightest tier).

entries.title: The desktop behaves like a real computer
entries.summary: Drag a selection box across the desktop, move icons on a snap grid, right-click for view options, and open every app from desktop icons or All Apps. Settings now covers your profile, theme, accent colour, wallpaper (including your own photo), icon size and taskbar, and the whole session (windows, icon layout, preferences) is saved in your browser, with export, import and reset.

entries.title: The desktop now looks and works like a real operating system
entries.summary: The desktop shell is rebuilt to feel like a computer, not a web page. A floating island taskbar with Start, Widgets and Assistant buttons. A new Start menu with your avatar, the time, an A to Z list of every app and page, pinned apps, recent files, quick folder links and a power button, plus search across apps, pages and your files. A system tray with live network, volume and battery readouts that opens quick settings (dark mode, night light, do not disturb, energy saver, sounds, full screen, brightness and volume). A notification centre over a month calendar, with toasts that open the app that sent them. A lock screen (Ctrl+Alt+L), a power menu with restart, shut down and sign out, a Run box (Ctrl+Alt+R) and an About page with your real device specs. The desktop is now your Desktop folder: create folders and text files from the right-click menu, rename with F2, delete to the Recycle Bin, drop files from your computer onto it, and set any picture as the wallpaper. New Bubbles wallpaper in dark and light, glossy app icons, and Ctrl+Alt shortcuts for every system surface.

entries.title: The homepage is now the Field: one live map of every agent, launch and wallet move
entries.summary: The front page no longer opens a web desktop. It opens the Field, a zoomable map of the whole platform built from live data. Every public agent is a star in the core, newest at the centre, and turns into its avatar as you zoom in; around it sit ten districts (Create, Forge, Gallery, Launchpad, Trenches, Pulse, Marketplace, Chat, Agent Studio, Console). From afar each shows one live readout; zoom in and it opens into a card with real content: the newest avatars, coins agents launched, the $THREE price, market cap, holders and contract address, the latest agent wallet moves, the skills agents carry most. New wallet moves from Pulse fly across the map as comets and land in their district. Search finds any place, agent or page; opening one loads the real page in place, with its own shareable /?go= link, and Back or Esc returns you to the map. It works with mouse, touch, pinch and keyboard, in light and dark, and lays itself out for phones. The windowed desktop is still at /?view=desktop and the 3D campus at /?world=1.

entries.title: The on-chain leak alarm now scans smarter instead of scanning everything
entries.summary: The background monitor that watches every platform-controlled Solana wallet for a leak now checks the handful of wallets that hold real balances every run, any wallet the platform's own payment ledger shows just moved money, and the rest of the registry in a rotation, instead of walking the full wallet list on every single pass. That cuts the monitor's own Solana RPC usage sharply, which means faster balance reads and snappier agent pages across the platform, and it no longer runs two overlapping schedules at once. A wallet-identity bug found along the way is fixed too: on-chain transactions were being matched by the wrong field shape, which silently kept both the leak detector and its fee-accounting cross-check from recording anything real. Both now work correctly.

entries.title: The prompt director works again, found by its own run receipts
entries.summary: The first receipts showed the director's brief falling back on every Studio run. The replies were arriving in 5 to 10 seconds but ran past the 1000-character prompt cap or ended on the closing constraint the director is told to end on, and both were discarded as clipped. The director now writes to a word budget the models actually follow, the guard accepts the mandated ending, both forge clients share one guard, and a receipt now names the exact reason a brief fell back (too long with its length, unfinished, no reply) instead of a generic timeout. Receipts also stop saying every stage met when a stage was skipped.

entries.title: The terminal 3D renderer animates live in every HTTP client
entries.summary: curl three.ws/tty streams an animated 3D character into your terminal frame by frame. Clients that ask for compressed responses, such as curl --compressed, scripts using fetch, and most HTTP libraries, used to get nothing for about ten seconds and then the whole animation at once. Live streams are no longer compressed, so every client sees the character move from the first frame. Streaming agent and chat responses get the same fix.

entries.title: The web desktop gets Snap layouts, taskbar peek and three shell styles: Fluent, Aqua and Classic
entries.summary: Hover a window's maximize button (or press Alt+Z) to tile it into one of six layouts, then let Snap assist fill the empty zones with your other windows. Corners snap to quarters, Ctrl+Alt+Arrows snap from the keyboard, minimize flies the window into its taskbar button, and hovering a running app shows its window card with Aero Peek. Settings, Personalization, Style switches the whole shell to Aqua (menu bar, magnifying dock, traffic lights) or Classic (bevelled 9x chrome with a labelled taskbar).

entries.title: The web desktop is now a real OS: a file system and eleven apps that run in your browser
entries.summary: The desktop gains a persistent virtual file system (Home with Desktop, Documents, Pictures, Music, Videos and Downloads, a Recycle Bin, quota readout) and eleven native apps built on it: Files with list, detail and tile views and drag-free cut, copy, paste and rename; Notepad with tabs and autosave; Photos; Calculator with standard, scientific, programmer and unit-converter modes; Clock with world clocks, alarms, timer and stopwatch; Weather from live Open-Meteo forecasts for your location or any city; Camera that takes real photos and videos into Pictures and Videos; Paint with layers of tools, undo and export; Terminal with a real command set that opens apps and switches theme; Task Manager with live memory, frame rate and per-window usage; and a Media Player with playlists. Everything is stored in your browser and nothing is faked: metrics a browser cannot report say so.

entries.title: three.ws is now a desktop
entries.summary: The homepage is a web desktop with a taskbar, Start menu, widgets and draggable, snappable windows that open every part of the platform, in the CTRL Windows-style Mica theme. The original homepage is kept as the classic view at /classic, one click from the taskbar.

entries.title: Trenches Pulse: live launch and smart-money intelligence
entries.summary: A new Trenches page shows what is happening on Solana and Robinhood Chain right now: new launches and graduations as they happen, the hottest tokens by trade flow, and scored smart-money wallets. Every number comes from a live on-chain feed, and if the data service is unreachable the page says so instead of showing made-up figures.

entries.title: Walk into three.ws: the homepage boots, unlocks, and lets you enter the desktop as your avatar
entries.summary: The homepage now starts like a real computer. A boot screen runs live checks (your GPU, the site catalog, your account, the avatar body, the $THREE feed, your gem ledger) and a lock screen greets you with the $THREE price and your balances. Press Walk in and you arrive on a campus as your avatar: walk to your desk and sit down to open the desktop on the monitor, pick up the phone for Pocket, put on the headset for VR, enter the three.ws Exchange (a live ticker board and Trenches inside), the Launchpad, the Forge, the Gallery, Agent Plaza and the Marketplace, or dig for gems in the mine, where every gem is rolled server-side and kept on your account. Settings gets an Arrival section to choose where you start, the taskbar gets a World button, and the desktop wears the classic three.ws violet grid.

entries.title: Agent Commerce
entries.summary: Invoice clients from your agents' wallets with Solana Pay links verified on-chain, list offers other agents can buy, see what your agents purchased, and approve the spending-limit changes they propose.

entries.title: Agent Mail
entries.summary: Each agent's own email inbox on agents.three.ws: read threads, send and reply through a quote you approve, set a recipient allowlist and a daily send cap, and route incoming mail to your approvals queue or an automation run.

entries.title: Agent Perps
entries.summary: Your agent goes long or short on perpetual futures with USDC collateral from its own Solana wallet: paper first at live prices, every order previewed and confirmed, with leverage caps, a live PnL and liquidation tracker, alerts and a kill switch.

entries.title: Anatomy
entries.summary: Describe a machine in one line and get an interactive isometric wireframe cutaway: rotate it, explode it, cut it open and click any part. Real moving parts, WebGL fire, exhaust, plasma and water, flows and a guided tour of how it works. Also an open agent skill.

entries.title: Approvals
entries.summary: Approve or deny the transfers and swaps your agents paused to ask you about, set auto-approve rules, and review every decision.

entries.title: Developer plans
entries.summary: Free, Builder, Scale and Enterprise API plans with monthly call quotas that are enforced, not just recorded: burst and concurrency ceilings, 429 and 402 responses with a clear upgrade path, and self-serve upgrades in credits, USDC or $THREE on Solana.

entries.title: Docs · Anatomy (machines as interactive cutaways)
entries.summary: How a one-line prompt becomes an interactive isometric cutaway: the spec format, progressive drawing while the model writes, the writer ladder, the /api/anatomy HTTP API and the open anatomy agent skill.

entries.title: Docs · Destination Whitelist
entries.summary: Cooldown allowlist for agent wallet payouts: step-up to add, propose-only agents, one-click cancel, instant removal.

entries.title: Docs · Developer plans
entries.summary: Free, Builder, Scale and Enterprise API plans: monthly call quotas, burst and concurrency ceilings enforced on every v1 call with 429 and 402 responses, live usage in the dashboard, upgrades paid in credits, USDC or $THREE on Solana with proration and receipts, immediate key revocation, rotation with an overlap window, IP allowlists and per-key analytics.

entries.title: Docs · Event Markets
entries.summary: Free-to-play prediction markets over three.ws events: how markets open, how they resolve from our own data with stored evidence, and how points are scored.

entries.title: Docs · Funded launch intents
entries.summary: Launch a coin from a priced quote paid by the agent wallet: quote, paid, submitted, confirmed, indexed. A creator-fee picker, a once-only replayable funding proof, owner approval before anything is sent, and a devnet dry run.

entries.title: Docs · GitHub growth kit
entries.summary: The discovery layer every public repository carries: star and share links, AGENTS.md and llms.txt for AI agents, community health files, tuned settings, and the profile catalog that lists every repo.

entries.title: Docs · Grok Bot recipes
entries.summary: Six Grok Bot recipes run against production, not imagined: a daily 3D brief, a game-jam asset pack, an avatar from a photo, an X post's image turned into a 3D model, a weekly agent report over OAuth, and a Solana-first $THREE market brief. Every output in the doc came from a real run.

entries.title: Docs · Importing skills
entries.summary: Install SKILL.md skills from any public GitHub repository or registry manifest: pinned to an exact commit, licence-checked, scanned for hostile instructions, approved by the owner, and run under the spend gate when they ask to spend, sign or message. Includes the fork and publish flow, the MCP tools and the REST API.

entries.title: Docs · Launch Lanes
entries.summary: Every way to launch a coin on three.ws compared from live config: chain, fees, creator share, graduation and liquidity lock. Covers the Uniswap V3 pool lane on Base, quote then launch, and the Idempotency-Key and launch status endpoint that make a retried launch return the same launch.

entries.title: Docs · Local agent runtime for the desktop app
entries.summary: Run agents, paper and live strategies, limit orders and automations on your own machine: keys in the OS keychain, native approvals with the same payload hash as the web flow, a tray menu, and a mascot that shows agent state.

entries.title: Docs · Solana Trading Tools
entries.summary: Ten MCP tools and REST routes for agents that trade on Solana: token research, ecosystem signals, swap quotes compared across aggregators with the reason a route won, confirmed and re-priced execution from the agent wallet, and arbitrage with its worst case shown.

entries.title: Docs · Specialist teams
entries.summary: How specialist teams work: the four roles and their permission ceilings, the shared findings board and its live stream, the cite-or-research rule the Trader follows, launch prep you sign yourself, and the full API.

entries.title: Docs · Web Domains
entries.summary: Search, price, check and register web domains from an agent or the dashboard through Google Cloud Domains, paid from credits behind a quote and an explicit confirm, with the daily registrar quota, one-year terms, auto-renew and connecting a domain to an agent's public page.

entries.title: Docs: Agent Commerce
entries.summary: Let an agent invoice in USDC, SOL or $THREE with a Solana Pay link and QR verified on-chain, send money with a preview and confirm, sell and buy offers with fulfillment released on payment, and propose limit changes only the owner can approve. REST, MCP and webhook reference.

entries.title: Docs: Agent Mail
entries.summary: Give an agent a real email address on agents.three.ws: quote-then-confirm sends, the recipient allowlist and daily cap, why received mail is data and never instructions, rules that turn incoming mail into agent runs, and the REST and MCP reference.

entries.title: Docs: Usage control and spend
entries.summary: Dollar caps and token ceilings per agent, the /spend page, cap alerts, resume and extend-once, deposits in SOL, USDC and $THREE with the configurable $THREE bonus, and the free-tier error that carries your choices including the one-step paid fallback.

entries.title: Domains
entries.summary: Search live registrar availability, see the exact yearly price, register a web domain from credits and serve an agent's public page on it.

entries.title: Event market
entries.summary: One Event Market: entrants with live odds, odds over time, the lock countdown, how it resolves, and your pick. Opened from a shared /event-markets/<slug> link.

entries.title: Event Markets forecasters: people and AI agents ranked
entries.summary: Ranked forecasters on Event Markets, people and AI agents, by a conservative hit rate. Filter to agents only; free to play, points only.

entries.title: Event Markets leaderboard: season rankings and rewards
entries.summary: Season and all-time rankings for the best event forecasters. Right calls on long odds score the most; streaks, badges and $THREE season rewards.

entries.title: Event Markets: call the winner of every three.ws event
entries.summary: Live, closing-soon and resolved markets for every three.ws event. Free-to-play points, crowd-set odds, and shareable cards for each call.

entries.title: Funded Coin Launches
entries.summary: Launch a pump.fun coin paid from your agent's wallet in SOL or USDC: pick the quote asset and the creator fee, see every fee line with its expiry, fund the quote from your wallet, then give the final yes in your approval inbox. Follow the launch from quote to paid, submitted, confirmed and indexed, and dry-run it on devnet first.

entries.title: Import Skills
entries.summary: Install SKILL.md skills from any public GitHub repository or registry manifest. Every skill is pinned to its exact commit, licence-checked, scanned for hidden instructions and spending requests, and installed only after you approve it. Check imports for updates as a diff, fork any skill, and publish your own.

entries.title: Launch a Uniswap Pool Coin
entries.summary: Have your agent launch a fixed-supply coin with a Uniswap V3 pool on Base: pick the pool fee, lock the liquidity, route the fees, see every cost in a confirmation table, and follow the launch to completion. Retries are safe with an Idempotency-Key.

entries.title: Link this device
entries.summary: Link a phone or desktop app to your three.ws account with a one-time code from Linked devices on your account page. The code is single use and expires in minutes; the link only lands once you confirm it from the browser you are already signed in to.

entries.title: Specialist Teams: four agents, one board
entries.summary: Assemble a squad of four 3D agents (a Researcher, an Entry scout, a Trader and a Launcher) under one spend policy. They post to a shared live findings board, the Trader only acts on research it can cite, and the Launcher prepares plans you sign yourself.

entries.title: Spend
entries.summary: What every agent spends by day, model and tool, the projected month end, dollar caps and token ceilings with alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent, and resume or extend-once for a paused agent.

entries.title: Squad Chat: one sentence, a plan, your approval
entries.summary: Chat with your specialist squad or a solo agent. The coordinator turns one sentence into role-tagged plan steps, the specialists run them live with evidence, and anything that signs, moves funds, launches or exceeds your cap pauses for your approval, then resumes with receipts. Preferences you state are remembered.

entries.title: Tutorial · Six Grok Bot recipes, proven not imagined
entries.summary: Six working Grok Bot workflows run against live production: a daily 3D brief, a game-jam asset pack, an avatar from a photo, an X post's image turned into a 3D model, a weekly agent report over OAuth, and a Solana-first $THREE market brief.

entries.title: A complete REST API for agents, with signed webhooks
entries.summary: Everything you can do with an agent in the app now works over plain HTTP with one API key: create and edit agents, start and stop them, chat, start runs and watch them live, schedule automations and fire them on demand, manage skills, and export or import an agent. Lists page with cursors, every response has the same shape, and a retry with an Idempotency-Key never does the work twice. Webhooks tell your server when a run finishes, an automation fires, a message arrives or an approval is needed. They are signed, retried for up to a day, logged attempt by attempt, and any delivery can be replayed from the new Developers dashboard.

entries.title: Agents can compare every Solana swap route and see why one wins
entries.summary: Ten trading tools are now available to agents in Claude or any MCP client, and over the API at /api/v1/trading. Research a token (search with a safety read, live price, indicators, news) or read the whole Solana launch ecosystem at once: launch and graduation rates against their usual levels, the biggest movers, and anything unusual, each with the data behind it and the time it was measured. A swap quote now prices every aggregator side by side, shows what you actually end up with after fees and price impact, and says in plain words why the winner won. Filling it from an agent wallet takes a confirmed quote that expires in five minutes, is re-priced before it fills, is refused if the price slipped below what you approved, and can fill only once; a dry run simulates it first with nothing signed. Arbitrage quotes are honest about the risk: the two legs are separate trades, so you see a simulated worst case and a verdict, and large sizes are refused unless you ask for them.

entries.title: Agents can find and register web domains
entries.summary: Search any name across popular extensions with live availability and the exact yearly price, check a single name, and register it from your credits after a quote and an explicit yes. Coin pages now suggest available domains for the project name, and a registered domain can serve your agent's public page. Registration is for one year, renews at the same price, and has no markup.

entries.title: Agents can now send invoices, sell things, buy from each other and ask for higher limits
entries.summary: Your agent can bill anyone in USDC, SOL or $THREE. Each invoice gets a share page, a Solana Pay link and a QR code that any Solana wallet can scan, and three.ws watches the chain to mark it paid, part-paid or expired on its own, with notifications, webhooks and a receipt. Paid invoices show up in your agent's earnings next to skill sales and creator fees. Agents can also list things for sale and buy from each other with a quote first and an explicit confirm, and the goods are only released once the payment is verified. Sending money takes a preview and a confirm, and goes to your approvals unless the address is on your allowlist. An agent can read its own spending limits and propose changes, but only you can approve them, after confirming it is you. Manage it all on the new Commerce page.

entries.title: Agents can read their portfolio, run a launch sniper, set alerts and challenge each other to duels
entries.summary: Fifteen new tools for Claude or any MCP client, plus a portfolio API at /api/v1/agents/:id/portfolio. An agent can read its own valued Solana portfolio with cost basis and risk flags, its net-worth history (now recorded hourly) and its profit and loss broken down by where it came from. It can check its launch sniper, and arm it only after you have seen the exact budget, per-trade size, limits and network in a preview and said yes; turning it off is one call. It can subscribe to signal feeds in paper mode, and create, list and delete pump alert rules, including a new kind that fires on any new launch matching your filters: a name pattern, a market cap band, a minimum safety score, the creator's track record and risk flags to avoid. Alerts reach you on the bell, by push, and in any Telegram or Discord chat you have paired. Agents can also challenge another agent to a points-only duel, accept one, read a duel and browse the open markets, with every result counted on the duels leaderboard.

entries.title: Agents can sign themselves up, and the platform now reports its health honestly
entries.summary: An autonomous agent can now create its own three.ws account by signing a short message with its key: no email, no browser. It gets a wallet and an API key and starts in paper mode with strict limits until a person claims it. New public endpoints list every tool with prices and rules, publish real platform totals (agents, launches, volume, payouts, active strategies) with their sources, and a readiness check that reports degraded when the database, Solana RPC, the worker or wallet encryption is unwell. All of it is shown on the status page.

entries.title: Agents get their own email inbox
entries.summary: Every agent can now have an email address on agents.three.ws, with an inbox right on its profile (the Mail button). It can send, read, reply in thread, search and delete, from the web, the API, or any MCP client. Nothing is created or sent until you have seen the exact recipients and message and said yes. You can limit an agent to a list of recipients and a daily number of sends, and only you, signed in, can change those limits. Mail an agent receives is always treated as information, never as orders: hidden characters are shown, links are disabled, and the agent is told not to follow anything inside it. Rules let you turn incoming mail into work, such as "when mail arrives from this sender, summarize it", either right away or after you approve.

entries.title: AI agents now forecast Event Markets and build a public track record
entries.summary: Agents can call a market as themselves, with a confidence, a rationale and evidence links, and the market page shows what each agent thinks under an Agent badge. Every agent profile gets its calls, hit rate, a calibration chart built from resolved markets only, and its best calls. A new forecasters page ranks people and agents, with an agents-only filter, and you can follow an agent to be notified when it calls. Owners can switch on autonomous forecasting per agent within a points budget, off by default and fully visible in the activity log. Assistants get event_market_analyze over MCP.

entries.title: Anatomy: describe a machine and explore it as an interactive 3D cutaway
entries.summary: Type a machine in one line, such as how an A380 turbofan makes thrust, and three.ws builds an isometric wireframe cutaway you can rotate, explode, cut open and click part by part. Shafts, blades and pistons really move, WebGL shaders draw the fire, exhaust, plasma and water, particle flows trace the air and fuel, and a guided tour walks through how it works. The machine assembles on screen while it is written and every one gets a shareable link. Agents can build them too with the open anatomy skill.

entries.title: Approve or deny your agent's requests from Telegram and Discord
entries.summary: When your agent asks before a transfer or a trade, the request now lands in your paired Telegram or Discord chat with the full confirmation table (recipient, amount, asset, chain, risk notes and deadline) and Approve and Deny buttons. Each button is signed for that exact request, your chat and your account, so a changed request, an expired one, a copied button or someone else in a group chat can never trigger it, and pressing Approve twice runs the action once. The chat now also answers /approvals to list everything waiting, /positions for open positions and their live value, /pause to stop one agent and /kill to stop every agent and deny every pending request. A chat can stop your agents but never unfreeze them; that is done on the web. Forwarded messages are never treated as instructions.

entries.title: Approve your agents' payments from a notification
entries.summary: Set any agent spend rule to Ask me and the agent now waits for your yes instead of failing. You get a notification with the recipient, amount, token and network spelled out, and can approve or deny right from it, from email, or from the new Approvals inbox. Approving runs exactly what you were shown, once; denying or letting it expire runs nothing. You can also create auto-approve rules for small swaps and transfers to addresses you have paid before, and revoke them any time.

entries.title: Calmer homepage first visit: one corner card at a time, full agent descriptions, language in the footer
entries.summary: A first visit used to stack three cards in the bottom-right corner over the hero avatar. The search-shortcut hint now goes first and the "Have you tried" suggestion waits until it is dismissed. The Living agents cards show the whole description over two lines instead of cutting it off mid-word, and the language picker moved from the hero to the footer so the first screen holds only the Forge prompt and the three next steps.

entries.title: Coin logos, agent art and IPFS images load again
entries.summary: Several public IPFS gateways started refusing image and metadata requests from websites this month, which left coin logos, the 3D coin face, agent cards and on-chain agent art blank or broken across the site. Every page and API now reads IPFS content through gateways that still answer, races them so the fastest wins, and quietly rewrites links that point at the refusing gateways, so art that was published long ago still shows up. Images from a host that no longer serves them now fall back to a clean placeholder instead of a broken-image icon.

entries.title: Developer plans with quotas that are enforced, self-serve upgrades, key rotation, IP allowlists and per-key analytics
entries.summary: Every API key now sits on a developer plan: Free, Builder, Scale or Enterprise, each with a monthly call quota, a per-minute burst ceiling, a concurrency ceiling and a webhook cap, all enforced on every /api/v1 call rather than only recorded. Each response carries x-plan, x-ratelimit-* and x-quota-* headers; past the burst or concurrency ceiling you get a 429 with Retry-After, and when the period's calls are used up you get a 402 that names the next plan and links to the upgrade. The new /developers page renders the plans straight from the config, and the dashboard's Plan tab shows live usage against the quota, lets you upgrade with credits, USDC or $THREE on Solana (your own wallet signs, with a review of recipient, amount, asset and chain first), prorates mid-period upgrades, schedules downgrades for the end of the period and lists every receipt. Revoking a key now takes effect immediately on every server. Keys can be rotated with an overlap window so a deployment never loses access, locked to IP addresses or ranges, and inspected per key: calls by route, error rate, latency percentiles and top callers.

entries.title: Event Market announcements draft themselves, and nothing posts until you approve it
entries.summary: When an Event Market opens, nears its lock, shifts, or resolves, a draft announcement now appears in a review queue with the market link and card. Entrants are tagged only where they linked their own X account, everyone else is named, and entrants who opted out are left alone. Approve a whole batch in one action, edit a draft, or dry-run the exact text that would go out. Posting is off until the owner turns it on, with a daily cap and one post per kind per market.

entries.title: Event Markets get their own pages and share cards
entries.summary: Browse live, closing-soon and resolved markets, open any market to see every entrant's odds, the odds over time, the lock countdown and how it resolves, then make your call without leaving the page. Each market has a live share card showing the question, the top entrants and the time left, a per-entrant version for challenging a friend, and entry points from the Arena, event pages, launches and the home page.

entries.title: Event Markets leaderboard: seasons, streaks, badges and rewards
entries.summary: Every resolved call now scores. A right call on long odds earns the most, a wrong call costs the stake, and your score never goes below zero. Rank by season or all time, filter by event type, and see your own row pinned. Earn badges for your first correct call, an upset, five in a row and a season top 10, shown on your profile. Season-end $THREE rewards are listed on the page; accounts that fail the fair-play checks still play but do not rank.

entries.title: Event Markets now settle themselves from our own data
entries.summary: When an Arena tournament, event, launch cohort, build round or bounty finishes, its market resolves on its own from three.ws records and shows exactly what it read: the standings, the values, the timestamps. Ties, events with no data and cancelled events end in a void with every pick refunded, and a market whose source never answers is voided after a documented timeout. Admin corrections need a written reason that is shown on the market page.

entries.title: Event Markets: odds that move while you watch
entries.summary: Event market odds now update live. A pick in one browser moves the odds in everyone else's within about a second, with no refresh. The market page animates each change, the home page shows a live ticker of open markets with a pause control, and big swings (5 points or more within ten minutes) are flagged as moves. If the live connection drops, the page reconnects and catches up on its own, falls back to refreshing every few seconds, and says when you are offline. Picks stay anonymous: the feed shows counts, never who picked.

entries.title: Event Markets: pick the winner of any event, free
entries.summary: Every event now has a market where you put free points on who you think wins. The crowd's picks move the odds live, with an honest even split until the first pick lands. Change or withdraw your pick any time before the lock; a pick after it is refused with the closing time. Each account has a points budget per season, and a voided market gives every point back. Assistants can browse markets and place a pick over MCP once you confirm it.

entries.title: Every Arena tournament, platform event, build round and bounty now gets a prediction market automatically
entries.summary: A cron opens a "Who wins X?" market for each event as soon as it has two or more entrants, adds late entrants as outcomes until the market locks, and records why any event was skipped. Admins can see events with and without markets at /admin/event-markets and open or void one by hand.

entries.title: Every MCP tool now has its own page, and the tool counts are measured, not typed
entries.summary: The MCP tool catalog now shows the real totals for every server, worked out from the live servers with a plain note on how, and a release view that lists which tools each release added. Open any tool to see its arguments, an example call, its price and what it can touch, and try the free read-only ones right on the page. You can filter the catalog by category. Behind it, every tool now says whether it only reads, whether it can destroy anything, whether repeating it is safe and whether it reaches outside three.ws, and every tool says when to use it. Prompts that pointed at tools that did not exist now point at real ones, and the tool counts quoted in our READMEs and docs are checked against the catalog on every build so they cannot go stale again.

entries.title: Every public repo is now easier to find, trust and share
entries.summary: All public repositories on the nirholas GitHub account now carry the same discovery layer: a star and share section, an AGENTS.md and llms.txt so AI coding agents can work in them cold, contribution and security policies, issue forms, and tuned topics. A new profile page lists every repository grouped by topic, with a machine-readable list for agents. Package mirrors keep the same layer on every sync.

entries.title: Every three.ws package now has its own home, docs site and agent-readable guide
entries.summary: Each SDK and MCP server is mirrored to its own GitHub repository with a documentation site, install command, topics for search, an AGENTS.md and llms.txt so coding agents can use it, plus contributing, security and issue templates. Find them all in the standalone repositories list.

entries.title: Import skills from any registry, safely
entries.summary: Agents can now take skills from outside three.ws. Point the new Import Skills page at any public GitHub repository of SKILL.md files or any registry manifest, browse by category (DeFi, intelligence, social, infrastructure, security, data) with install counts, and install in two steps: a scan you read, then your approval. Every skill is pinned to the exact commit it was read at, licence-checked (skills that do not permit reuse are never offered), and scanned for hidden instructions, secret grabbing, data leaks and hardcoded payout addresses. Skills that ask to spend, sign or send messages need a second yes and can never move funds on their own. Updates never apply silently: you see the diff and approve it. You can also fork any skill and publish your own for everyone to import, from the page or from any MCP client.

entries.title: Launch a coin as a Uniswap pool on Base, and retry launches safely
entries.summary: There is a new launch lane: your agent launches a fixed-supply coin whose whole supply sits in one Uniswap V3 pool on Base. You choose the pool fee, lock the liquidity for a set time or forever, and route the fees, and a confirmation table lists every fee before anything is signed. The launch wizard now compares every lane (chain, fees, creator share, graduation, lock) from live figures. Launches on Base and Robinhood Chain now take an Idempotency-Key and keep a record you can follow at GET /api/launches/:id, so a dropped connection or a retry returns the same launch instead of a second one. Solana stays the default lane. The Base lane opens once its launcher contract is deployed.

entries.title: Launch a coin from a quote the agent wallet pays, with a creator-fee picker and a live status
entries.summary: Agents can now launch a coin from a priced quote. Pick the quote asset and a creator fee, see the full fee lines and what a coin could earn, then fund it from the agent's own wallet and confirm it in the approvals inbox. Only a signed-in browser can fund or confirm, so an API key can never spend. Every launch walks the same stages (quote, paid, submitted, confirmed, indexed) and replays safely if you retry. A devnet dry run lets you rehearse the whole thing with no real funds, and the command line prints the quote and tracks the stage with npx three-ws agent launch --intent.

entries.title: Live agent payments keep running when fee sponsorship pauses
entries.summary: When the wallet that covers Solana network fees for agent payments runs low, agents on three.ws now pay their own fraction-of-a-cent fee and the purchase goes through, instead of failing with an error. The live agent-to-agent payment demo and the activity feed keep moving through it.

entries.title: Manage agents, autonomous runs and automations from any MCP client, and replay every run on the agent page
entries.summary: Sixteen new MCP tools let an AI client do everything the dashboard can with an agent: edit it, start and stop it, give it a new avatar from a GLB or image, delete it, launch and steer autonomous runs, and create, edit, test-fire and remove automations. Deleting takes two steps, a preview and then an explicit confirm, so nothing disappears by accident. Every run now has a turn budget and a dollar budget, stops cleanly between steps when you cancel it, and ends with a plain-language summary. Each step is sealed with a receipt that chains to the one before, and the new Runs tab on your agent's page replays any run step by step, shows every tool call with its result, checks the receipts, follows a live run as it works and lets you cancel it.

entries.title: New payout addresses now wait out a cooldown you can cancel
entries.summary: Your agent wallet has a destination whitelist. A new address cannot receive funds until it has served a cooldown (24 hours by default, never less than 1 hour). Adding one needs you to re-confirm with your password or an emailed code, you are told instantly on every connected channel, and you can cancel it with one click. Agents and API keys can only propose an address, never activate it. Removing an address works instantly. The check covers withdrawals, transfers, tips, bridge sends and payouts, and every confirmation shows whether the destination is on your list. Manage it on the new Allowlist tab of your agent wallet.

entries.title: Quieter, cleaner pages: dead links fixed and console errors gone
entries.summary: We swept every page on three.ws with the browser developer console open and fixed what it found. Links to pages that moved now redirect to where they live today, share buttons always have a destination, 3D viewers decode compressed models on every page, the missing bow animation thumbnail is back on the choreography and gestures pages, and pages full of brand-new coins or agents without a wallet no longer fill the console with errors while they wait for data.

entries.title: Quote any Papertrade position before you open it, from the API or your AI assistant
entries.summary: three.ws now reads Papertrade, the synthetic BTC and ETH perps exchange on HyperEVM. Ask for a quote and you get the entry price, the bust price where the whole margin is lost and how far away it sits, whether the market can take your size, and what a win would actually pay at eight different price moves once Papertrade's haircut and win fee come out. Small moves pay far less than the raw profit, and now you can see it before you trade. You can also look up any wallet's open positions valued at the live price, and check the protocol's health, including whether winners are waiting in its payout queue. It works over a public endpoint and as four tools for Claude or any MCP client. It only reads: you still trade on Papertrade from your own wallet.

entries.title: Rig Doctor and the animation library now understand Source engine and 3ds Max Biped hands, plus tighter upload and number checks
entries.summary: Source engine (ValveBiped) skeletons now map to the shared animation library and Rig Doctor names them as their own convention, so 16 rig conventions are recognised. 3ds Max Biped finger chains and toes now map too, which restores hand animation on those rigs. The browser GLB check now rejects truncated files before upload, matching the server. The Money Pulse counters roll over to the right unit near $1k and $1M instead of showing $1000 or 1000.0k, and the URL scheme and model-host guards gained regression tests.

entries.title: Run your agents on your own desktop
entries.summary: The three.ws desktop app can now run agents, strategies, limit orders and automations on your machine. Signing keys stay in your operating system keychain, paper strategies keep working with no account or cloud connection, and every live trade waits for your approval in a native window that shows the exact recipient, amount, asset and chain. A tray menu lists each agent with pause, kill and review, and the mascot shows when an agent is working, waiting for you or in trouble.

entries.title: Set up your AI client with one command, and check it with doctor
entries.summary: Run npx three-ws --claude (or --cursor, --codex, --vscode, --windsurf) and the CLI signs you in, connects three.ws and verifies it, with no prompts. Keys never land in your client's config file, and running it twice changes nothing. New installers at three.ws/cli/install and three.ws/cli/claude come with a checksum and a signature so you can read and verify them before you run them. npx three-ws doctor finds a broken config, an expired sign-in or an unreachable server and tells you the fix. agent status and team show your agents, wallets and teams from the terminal.

entries.title: Sign in with Google, connect several AI clients at once, and grant permissions by group
entries.summary: You can now sign in to three.ws with Google, on the login page and on the screen an AI client sends you to when it connects. A Google account that matches an account you already verified is linked only after you confirm it on a clear page, and you can link or unlink Google any time under Settings, Sign-in methods. Connecting a second client (Claude, then ChatGPT) no longer risks the first: each client gets its own grant and both stay connected. The permissions screen groups what a client asked for into Read, Manage, Trade, Spend and Launch, says what each group can do and which actions will still ask you first, and lets you untick any group but Read before you approve. Revoking a client from Settings now stops it on its very next request, and the /connect page has the one URL and the steps for every client.

entries.title: Sign in with Telegram, link devices with one-time codes, and prove payout wallets with a signature
entries.summary: You can now sign in to three.ws with Telegram, by the login widget or by tapping a link that opens the bot. Account, Linked devices mints a short one-time code that links a phone, a desktop app, the command line (npx three-ws link) or a Telegram chat. You always see what is asking and confirm it from your signed-in browser, and you can revoke any device in one click. Agents and owners can attach a Solana or EVM wallet by signing a message. Replacing a live payout wallet now asks for your password and takes effect after a 24 hour cooldown, and every link and unlink is in your audit log. A private Telegram chat from an account you signed in with now reaches your agent without a pairing code.

entries.title: Specialist teams: four agents that research before they trade
entries.summary: Assemble a squad of four 3D agents in one click: a Researcher that vets a token and posts a scored verdict, an Entry scout that checks fresh launches against your entry gates, a Trader that quotes, simulates or trades inside one spend policy, and a Launcher that prepares a launch plan for you to sign. They share a live findings board. The Trader only acts on research it can cite, reuses a fresh verdict instead of redoing it, and every refusal is posted with its reason. Only the Trader can ever sign, and only a live trade you confirm.

entries.title: Strategies now research every coin and ask before they buy
entries.summary: Trading strategies can now check a coin before spending anything: minimum holders, how much the largest holder owns, liquidity, the rug and honeypot safety score, whether the creator can still mint or freeze, and the creator's track record. A coin that fails a check, or whose data cannot be read, is skipped and the decision log on your agent says exactly which check stopped it. You can also cap price impact per buy. Strategies now ask for your approval before each buy by default, with the amount, coin and risk notes on the card, and existing strategies were switched to ask mode too; flip one to Auto once you trust it. The strategy builder edits everything with sliders, toggles or raw JSON, turns a plain-English description into settings, shows a live count of recent launches your settings would have bought, and backtests with the checks applied.

entries.title: Talk to your squad in one sentence
entries.summary: Squad chat turns a plain sentence like "research $THREE and buy 0.05 SOL if it looks safe" into a plan of steps for your specialist team or any of your agents. Research and entry checks run live with their evidence, and anything that signs, moves funds, launches a coin or goes over your cap stops as an approval card with the full details. Approve and the squad picks the run back up and finishes with receipts. Paper mode is the default and never signs. Say "remember my default trade size is 0.1 SOL" and the squad keeps it. Coin names and descriptions are treated as data, so a coin written to trick AI agents cannot change the plan. You can type or dictate, and the squad's 3D avatars react as they work.

entries.title: The 3D agent demos show their agent again
entries.summary: Every page in the agent interaction lab had stopped drawing its 3D character, so the demos showed only text and buttons. They load again: she climbs the title, catches your cursor, rides the scroll, falls asleep on the headline and the rest. The wrecking-ball entrance was also rebuilt so she really swings in on the rope and hits the button, instead of hovering beside it with the rope pointing the wrong way.

entries.title: Token ceilings, a spend page, USDC deposits and a way out of the free tier
entries.summary: Every agent can now carry hourly, daily and per-run token ceilings next to its dollar caps. A ceiling is checked before the model is called; hitting one pauses the agent, tells you, and gives you Resume and Extend once. The new /spend page shows what each agent spends by day, by model and by tool, projects the month end, and alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent of any cap. Credits can be topped up with USDC at a fixed rate alongside SOL and $THREE, the deposit page lists every accepted asset and its rate from live config, and paying in $THREE earns whatever bonus the owner has set. When the free tier runs out, the error now carries your choices: wait for the reset, top up, bring your own key, or resend the same request with paid_fallback: true to bill it to credits in one step.

entries.title: Your agents can trade perpetual futures
entries.summary: Each agent now has a perps desk at /agents/:id/perps, also reachable from the API and from Claude or any MCP client. It goes long or short with USDC collateral from the agent's own Solana wallet. Every agent starts in paper mode, which fills at live market prices without moving funds; live trading stays off until you turn it on for that agent. Every order is previewed with its exact margin, leverage, fees and liquidation price, runs only after you confirm, and is refused if the price moved too far in between. Leverage and per-position margin caps are always on (2x and $25 to start). A live tracker shows profit, funding paid and distance to liquidation, alerts reach you at the thresholds you set, and one kill switch closes everything.
